about.title: Dixon Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Dixon is a small city, but its business corridors along West A Street and near I-80 see steady foot traffic — grocery stores, gas stations, restaurants, and apartment complexes where spills, uneven walkways, and poor lighting can turn an ordinary errand into a fall. Unlike a car crash, a fall on someone else's property doesn't always come with an obvious point of blame. California law requires showing the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to fix it or warn you. That's why what happens in the minutes and days after your fall matters so much — photos of the spilled liquid, the broken step, the missing mat, and any surveillance footage before it's overwritten. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results. We simply connect Dixon residents and visitors who were hurt on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can evaluate the notice question and help preserve evidence while it still exists.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Fall in Dixon

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires proof the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records that speak to that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Dixon stores and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California's pure comparative fault rule means even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you can still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts fairly instead of letting an insurer assign you all the blame.

items.question: I fell in a store on West A Street in Dixon. What should I do first?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of exactly what caused the fall — the wet floor, the torn carpet, the uneven pavement — before it gets cleaned up or fixed. Report the fall to a manager and ask for an incident report, and try to get the names of any witnesses. An attorney can later request the store's surveillance footage before it's routinely deleted.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall, but if the property is owned by a public entity — like a city building or school — that deadline is much shorter and involves an earlier claims process. Because Dixon has both private businesses and public facilities, it's worth having someone confirm which timeline applies to your situation quickly.

items.question: What if the store says I was watching my phone and wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rule means you can still pursue a claim even if you share some responsibility for the fall; your recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault. Insurers often raise this argument early, so having an independent attorney review the full picture — including whether the hazard should have been fixed or marked — can help balance that narrative.
